edition.locus: Gebhardt XII.VI (nails; the chariot prayer; amen)

source_text: Σκεψάμενος μετὰ τῶν συνέδρων αὐτοῦ κελεύει ἥλους γενέσθαι ὑπὸ ἄρθρων καὶ καθηλώσας τοὺς πόδας τοῦ μάρτυρος ἐποίησεν ἔμπροσθεν προτρέχειν αὐτὸν τοῦ ἅρματος αὐτοῦ. Καὶ ἐλαυνόμενος δυσὶν φραγελλίοις οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίνατο, ἀλλ᾽ ἔψαλλεν λέγων· Ὑπομένων ὑπέμεινα τὸν κύριον, καὶ προσέσχεν μοι καὶ εἰσήκουσεν τῆς δεήσεώς μου. Ὡς δὲ ἐπλησίασεν τῷ ἐμπορίῳ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα ὀλιγοψυχῶν ἐκ τοῦ κόπου ὁ μακάριος Κόνων καὶ ἀναβλέψας πρὸς τὸν ἑαυτοῦ δεσπότην ἐπηύξατο λέγων· Κύριε Ἰησοῦ Χριστέ, δέξαι τὴν ψυχήν μου καὶ ῥῦσαί με ἀπὸ τῶν αἱμοβόρων κυνῶν καὶ ἀνάπαυσόν με μετὰ πάντων τῶν δικαίων σου τῶν πεποιηκότων τὸ θέλημά σου, ναί, ὁ θεός μου, βασιλεὺς τῶν αἰώνων. Καὶ ταῦτα εὐξάμενος καὶ σφραγίσας ἑαυτὸν εὐθέως ἀπέδωκεν τὸ πνεῦμα. Ὁ δὲ παράνομος ἡγεμών, πολλὰ καταπλαγεὶς ἐπὶ τῇ νίκῃ τοῦ μάρτυρος, ἐξώρμησεν ἐπὶ τὸν ἴδιον δρόμον. Ὁ δὲ μακάριος Κόνων προσφορὰ προσηνέχθη τῷ βασιλεῖ τῶν αἰώνων Θεῷ· ᾧ ἡ δόξα εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων, ἀμήν.
pass_a_gloss: Literal sense: having taken counsel with his assessors he commands nails to come to be beneath the joints, and after nailing through the feet of the martyr he caused him to run forward in front of his own chariot. And while being driven by two whips he answered nothing, but was chanting a psalm, saying: waiting I waited for the Lord, and he gave heed to me and heard my entreaty. And when he drew near to the market-place the blessed Conon, putting his knees down and losing heart from the toil, and looking up to his own Master prayed, saying: Lord Jesus Christ, receive my soul and rescue me from the blood-devouring dogs and give me rest with all your righteous ones who have done your will, yes, my God, king of the ages. And after praying these things and sealing himself he immediately gave up his spirit. But the lawless governor, much struck with astonishment at the victory of the martyr, rushed off upon his own course. And the blessed Conon was offered as an offering to God the king of the ages, to whom be glory unto the ages of the ages, amen.
pass_b_english: After deliberating with his councillors, he ordered nails to be fashioned to pass beneath the joints, and when he had nailed the martyr's feet through, he forced him to run on foot ahead in front of his own chariot. And though driven onward by two lashes, he made no answer, but sang a psalm, saying, With waiting I waited for the Lord, and he inclined to me and heard my supplication (Psalm 40:1). And when he came near the market-place, the blessed Conon sank to his knees, faint with exhaustion, and lifted his eyes to his own Master and prayed, saying, Lord Jesus Christ, receive my soul, and deliver me from the bloodthirsty dogs, and grant me rest with all your righteous who have done your will, yes, my God, King of the ages.

And when he had prayed these words and signed himself with the seal, at once he yielded up his spirit. But the lawless governor, greatly confounded by the martyr's victory, hastened away upon his own road. And the blessed Conon was presented as an offering to God, the King of the ages, to whom be glory unto the ages of ages, amen.

choices.english: nails to be fashioned to go under the joints
choices.why: ὑπὸ with accusative gives position under the joints, and γενέσθαι marks manufacture for that purpose, so the nails are fitted beneath the foot-joints rather than simply made by the joints.
rejected: nails to come into being by means of joints

choices.term: ἐποίησεν ἔμπροσθεν προτρέχειν αὐτὸν τοῦ ἅρματος αὐτοῦ
choices.english: he forced him to run ahead in front of his chariot
choices.why: ποιεῖν with infinitive is causative compulsion here, and the double fronting ἔμπροσθεν plus genitive τοῦ ἅρματος stresses exposure before the moving chariot.
dative of arrival after ἐπλησίασεν points to a public commercial place where the procession ends, not commerce in the abstract.

choices.english: was brought forward as an offering
choices.why: cognate noun plus aorist passive verb makes a solemn liturgical claim that his death was a presentation to God, not merely that he was carried somewhere.
